units.heading: Cooperative apiary handbook
units.own_text: This handbook collects independent work instructions and building information for the cooperative apiary. Each named procedure has its own scope.

units.heading: Moving occupied hives
units.own_text: The instructions in this section apply only to occupied hives moved between stands inside the same apiary. Moving a hive to another site requires a separate transport plan.

units.heading: Entrance preparation
units.own_text: Close the hive entrance with a ventilated transport screen after the last flying bees have returned. Keep the screen unobstructed throughout the move.

units.heading: Securing the boxes
units.own_text: Fasten the hive boxes and floor together with two ratchet straps before lifting. Lift the secured hive with two people and place it level on the new stand.

units.heading: Reopening
units.own_text: Remove the transport screen after the hive is stable on its new stand. Place a leafy branch across the entrance to encourage returning bees to reorient.

units.heading: Trolley paint
units.own_text: The equipment trolley is painted cream. Touch-up paint and brushes are kept in the garden shed; paint colour does not identify a hive's destination.

units.heading: Queen inspection exception
units.own_text: An occupied hive awaiting completion of a queen inspection must not be moved between stands, even when the entrance has been screened and the boxes are strapped. Complete and record the queen inspection before scheduling the move.

units.heading: Visitor badges
units.own_text: Visitors collect yellow paper badges from reception and return them before leaving. Badges do not record hive health or inspection status.

units.heading: Textile conservation room
units.own_text: The following record concerns quarantine of woven museum textiles in the conservation room, not furniture or paper collections.

units.heading: Intake notebook
units.own_text:
The conservation room occupies the upper floor of the east wing. A stone staircase leads from the entrance lobby to the corridor outside the room. The staircase has a wooden rail along its inner edge. Visitors use the lobby telephone to announce their arrival. A member of staff meets them at the bottom of the staircase and accompanies them upstairs. Coats and bags remain in the lobby lockers. Each locker has a small brass number attached to its door. Lost locker keys are reported to reception. The reception counter contains a shallow drawer for spare name cards. Name cards are written with a broad black pen so that they can be read from across the lobby. Empty card boxes are flattened before they are placed in the recycling container. The recycling container stands under the counter but must not obstruct the staff footrest. A wooden notice frame on the opposite wall displays the opening hours. The frame is removed from the wall for cleaning at the beginning of each season. Two screws hold the frame in place. The maintenance caretaker keeps the screwdriver in a locked tool cabinet. Only the caretaker opens that cabinet. The corridor has a row of tall windows overlooking a paved courtyard. The window blinds are raised for cleaning and lowered again afterwards. A pair of indoor shoes is available for each member of the housekeeping staff. The shoes remain on a low rack beside the service entrance. Their soles are brushed before they are returned to the rack. A bell at the service entrance alerts reception when a delivery arrives. The bell is checked during the weekly building inspection. Delivery drivers wait outside until a staff member opens the door. Empty delivery cartons are kept flat in the ground-floor storeroom. Cartons with torn corners are put aside for recycling rather than reused. The storeroom has a large wall calendar showing collection dates. The calendar is replaced at the beginning of January. The old calendar is removed rather than left underneath the new one. A round clock above the storeroom doorway has a plain white face. Its battery is replaced when the minute hand begins to stop. Spare clock batteries are stored in the office stationery cupboard. That cupboard also holds pencil sharpeners and paper clips. Paper clips are sorted by size into two small tins. The tins have lids to prevent their contents spilling into the drawer. A felt pad beneath each tin protects the wooden drawer base. The pads are shaken outdoors when dust accumulates. A cleaning cloth hangs from a peg near the office sink. The cloth is washed after use and dried before it is returned to the peg. The sink is not used for drinking water. Drinking water is available from a dispenser in the staff dining room. The dining room tables are wiped after every break. Staff return chairs to their marked positions before leaving the room. The floor markings leave a clear route between the entrance and the rear exit. The rear exit opens onto a covered walkway. During rain the walkway mat is replaced with a dry one at midday. Wet mats are hung in the utility yard rather than folded into a cupboard. These facilities observations are included for the building team and do not set quarantine release requirements.

A newly received woven textile must remain in a sealed quarantine cabinet for twenty-seven days. Release requires a conservator to record two pest-free inspections seven days apart. If live larvae are found at either inspection, restart the full twenty-seven-day quarantine after treatment instead of releasing the textile.

units.heading: Lighting inventory
units.own_text: The room has five ceiling lamps with frosted covers. Replacement covers are ordered through the buildings office.

units.heading: Cave team equipment guide
units.own_text: This guide contains separate equipment procedures and storeroom information for the cave survey team. A heading's instructions apply only to the equipment it names.

units.heading: Underground radio check
units.own_text: This procedure applies to the low-frequency radios used by the survey team below ground. Surface vehicle radios use a different check sheet.

units.heading: Antenna connection
units.own_text: Connect the loop antenna to the marked socket before enabling the transmitter. Lay the loop flat and keep its cable clear of the footpath.

units.heading: Voice exchange
units.own_text: Ask the surface operator to repeat the test phrase exactly and record the reply in the trip log. A carrier indication alone does not count as a completed radio check.

units.heading: Standby
units.own_text: After a successful voice exchange, place the transmitter in receive-only standby until the scheduled check-in. Leave the antenna connected during standby.

units.heading: Storage labels
units.own_text: The radio cases have orange inventory labels. Replacement labels are available in the stationery tray; their colour does not indicate battery charge or signal quality.

units.heading: Flood watch exception
units.own_text: During an active flood watch, the underground radio check does not authorize entering the cave even if the test phrase is repeated correctly. The expedition leader must formally clear the flood watch before entry.

units.heading: Membership forms
units.own_text: New team members submit membership forms to the secretary. Blank forms are printed on recycled paper and kept beside the visitor book.

units.heading: Community bakery notebook
units.own_text: This notebook describes the overnight sourdough fermentation used for the community bakery's rye loaves. Yeast-only dough follows another schedule.

units.heading: Overnight record
units.own_text:
The bakery building was converted from a village meeting hall. A small porch shelters the entrance door from rain. The porch contains a bench where visitors can wait for the shop to open. The bench is wiped each morning before the door is unlocked. A wooden board beside the door displays the shop opening times. The board is brought indoors before the building closes for the night. Its hanging cord is replaced when it becomes frayed. Spare cord is kept with the office packing materials. The office occupies a narrow room behind the sales counter. A desk stands against the wall beneath a framed map of the village. The map is decorative and is not used for delivery routing. Delivery routes are written on separate cards and handed to the driver. Cards from completed routes go into a labelled paper envelope. At the end of the month the envelope is placed in the records cupboard. The records cupboard has three shelves and a sliding door. The bottom shelf is reserved for empty envelopes and blank cards. The middle shelf holds completed records in date order. The upper shelf holds spare folders. A small step stool is provided for reaching that shelf. The stool is put away after use so that it does not obstruct the narrow passage. The passage leads to a shared washroom and the rear exit. The washroom notice asks visitors to report leaking taps to the shop assistant. The assistant records building faults in a notebook at the counter. Faults are reviewed with the landlord during the monthly building visit. The landlord enters through the rear yard rather than crossing the production area. The yard gate is kept closed except when a delivery vehicle is passing through it. A painted line marks the place where drivers should stop before unloading. The line is repainted when it becomes difficult to see. A stiff brush is stored beside the gate for clearing leaves from the drain cover. The brush is returned to its hook after use. The drain cover is lifted only by the building caretaker. The caretaker wears a numbered visitor badge while on the premises. Spare badges are stored in a small tray beneath the counter. The tray also holds a roll of adhesive labels for office parcels. Used parcel labels are crossed out before a carton is reused. Torn cartons are flattened and collected for recycling. The recycling collection takes place on alternate Wednesdays. A calendar near the rear door marks those Wednesdays with a blue circle. Staff check the calendar before placing cartons in the yard. Cartons remain indoors during heavy rain. The staff room contains a low bookcase with old local newspapers. Papers more than one month old are removed at the end of each week. A basket beside the bookcase holds lost gloves and scarves. Items left in the basket for three months are donated through the village office. The staff room curtains are laundered during the summer closure. While the curtains are away, plain paper screens cover the lower window panes. The screens are taken down when the clean curtains return. These notes record ordinary building administration and do not establish any dough fermentation time, temperature or release condition.

Hold the rye sourdough at eighteen degrees Celsius for eleven hours. Before dividing the dough, verify that its volume has increased by at least one half and record the observation. If pink streaks or a putrid smell are present, discard the entire batch; do not extend fermentation or blend it into fresh dough.

units.heading: Customer receipts
units.own_text: Duplicate customer receipts are filed by week in the sales office. Blank receipt rolls are stored under the counter.

The bench is wiped each morning before the door is unlocked. A wooden board beside the door displays the shop opening times. The board is brought indoors before the building closes for the night. Its hanging cord is replaced when it becomes frayed. Spare cord is kept with the office packing materials. The office occupies a narrow room behind the sales counter. A desk stands against the wall beneath a framed map of the village. The map is decorative and is not used for delivery routing. Delivery routes are written on separate cards and handed to the driver. Cards from completed routes go into a labelled paper envelope. At the end of the month the envelope is placed in the records cupboard. The records cupboard has three shelves and a sliding door. The bottom shelf is reserved for empty envelopes and blank cards. The middle shelf holds completed records in date order. The upper shelf holds spare folders. A small step stool is provided for reaching that shelf. The stool is put away after use so that it does not obstruct the narrow passage. The passage leads to a shared washroom and the rear exit. The washroom notice asks visitors to report leaking taps to the shop assistant. The assistant records building faults in a notebook at the counter. Faults are reviewed with the landlord during the monthly building visit. The landlord enters through the rear yard rather than crossing the production area. The yard gate is kept closed except when a delivery vehicle is passing through it. A painted line marks the place where drivers should stop before unloading. The line is repainted when it becomes difficult to see. A stiff brush is stored beside the gate for clearing leaves from the drain cover. The brush is returned to its hook after use. The drain cover is lifted only by the building caretaker. The caretaker wears a numbered visitor badge while on the premises. Spare badges are stored in a small tray beneath the counter. The tray also holds a roll of adhesive labels for office parcels. Used parcel labels are crossed out before a carton is reused. Torn cartons are flattened and collected for recycling. The recycling collection takes place on alternate Wednesdays. A calendar near the rear door marks those Wednesdays with a blue circle. Staff check the calendar before placing cartons in the yard. Cartons remain indoors during heavy rain. The staff room contains a low bookcase with old local newspapers. Papers more than one month old are removed at the end of each week. A basket beside the bookcase holds lost gloves and scarves. Items left in the basket for three months are donated through the village office. The staff room curtains are laundered during the summer closure. While the curtains are away, plain paper screens cover the lower window panes. The screens are taken down when the clean curtains return. These notes record ordinary building administration and do not establish any dough fermentation time, temperature or release condition.

Hold the rye sourdough at eighteen degrees Celsius for eleven hours. Before dividing the dough, verify that its volume has increased by at least one half and record the observation. If pink streaks or a putrid smell are present, discard the entire batch; do not extend fermentation or blend it into fresh dough.

units.heading: Customer receipts
units.own_text: Duplicate customer receipts are filed by week in the sales office. Blank receipt rolls are stored under the counter.

units.heading: Community bakery notebook
units.own_text: This notebook describes the overnight sourdough fermentation used for the community bakery's rye loaves. Yeast-only dough follows another schedule.
